hypothesis: A ClayCode frontier integration claim is valid only if the exact candidate is composed with the current canonical main tree before target execution; testing the PR head alone is insufficient once main advances.
strongest_counterhypothesis: The current-main delta is non-overlapping or semantically irrelevant, so head-only target evidence would remain representative of the eventual merge result.

fresh_overlap_observation.material_overlap: Current main had integrated PR #310/#343 package/evaluator paths also modified by the frontier candidate.

falsifier.gap: The existing ClayCode Frontier Integration VPS workflow selected github.event.pull_request.head.sha for pull_request runs and therefore exercised the branch head rather than a current-base composition.
falsifier.consequence: A green run could not by itself prove the actual main+candidate merge tree after main advanced.

repair.mechanism: Fetch exact branch head plus live refs/heads/main into run-owned /tmp state, merge head onto current main, fail on any unmerged path, bind merged tree identity, then execute the ClayCode package/differential/corpus/census gates.

architecture_delta.change: Current-main composition becomes an explicit fail-closed ClayCode integration invariant rather than an assumption derived from PR targeting.
architecture_delta.promotion_gate: Require accepted-target PASS on an exact current-main composed tree before scoped integration promotion.
architecture_delta.rollback: Revert the dedicated composition workflow and merge-resolution commit if it is shown to mis-model GitHub merge semantics; never replace it with head-only evidence.

negative_and_unknown_evidence: Cancelled workflows are not counted as ClayCode product failures.
WP04 Hosted Shadow is a real workflow failure but the job log blob was unavailable, so cause remains UNKNOWN.
Full ClayCode Frontier Integration run 31508062579 was still queued; no PASS is claimed.
external_primary_basis: GitHub REST Git tree/commit model: composed file trees are explicit Git objects and a commit can be created from a chosen tree with ordered parents.
